newsitem.title: USA: Republic Industries profits jump 132 Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Republic Industries profits jump 132 Philippines.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc. said Tuesday its profits jumped by 132 percent in the second quarter, during which it acquired two car rental companies and agreed to add a third to its growing automotive stable.

Republic, which bought Spirit Rent-A-Car Inc. and Value Rent-A-Car Inc. and agreed to buy Snappy Car Rental Inc. in the quarter, said its net income increased to $69.5 million, or 17 cents a share, from $30.0 million, or 9 cents a share.

The company, which owns the nation's largest chain of new vehicle dealerships and is building a chain of used car megastores, said revenues for the three months ended June 30 increased 59 percent to $2.38 billion from $1.50 billion.
For the six months ended June 30, Republic said, net income increased 115 percent to $102.3 million, or 26 cents a share, from $47.5 million, or 15 cents a share.
Revenue for the six months increased 50 percent to $4.15 billion from $2.77 billion.

The company, which also has subsidiaries in the solid waste and electronic security industries, said operating income, before restructuring and non-recurring expenses, increased to $103.3 million for the latest three months.

During the period, Republic recorded a $102.3 million pre-tax gain from the sale of 15 million shares of ADT Ltd and recorded a $94.1 million pre-tax charge related to the integration of its automotive rental companies.
Republic's stock lost 6 cents to $24.94 in late composite trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
